round_trip_and_identity_invariants: ASTRecord deserializes from both its closed mapping and canonical JSON forms to the identical record; canonical bytes, the closed DAG-JSON payload, and the record CID must agree, and CID verification recomputes that identity.

The AST schema registry is exact-version-only, immutable, and canonically ordered; unknown fields, ambiguous versions, duplicate JSON keys, floats, noncanonical forms, dangling/cyclic records, and CID tampering reject rather than minting an alternate authority.

PythonASTExtractor binds its normalized facts, toolchain/frontend name and version, source provenance, and shared schema into a golden CID; output remains byte-identical across fresh processes with different PYTHONHASHSEED values.

Stable symbol identity binds repository, language, normalized module path, qualified name, kind, and namespace. Version identity additionally binds position-free normalized AST, signature, decorators, annotations, extractor identity/version, semantic-index schema, and property role.

Formatting and unrelated fields do not change logical identity or position-free version CID, while a forged normalized AST cannot retain the previous version CID; NaN is rejected before content hashing and signed/nonfinite literal representations remain distinguished.

The compiler parses source and does not import or execute it. Dynamic execution, reflection, constructed attributes, native boundaries, monkey patches, metaclass mutation, and runtime code generation are downgraded rather than claimed exact.
